les: Wat alles in ons water beland
kaps_punt: Waterbesoedeling: in die omgewing, kan baie dinge meng of oplos in water; water kan besoedel word deur: onoplosbare stowwe, soos olie, plastiek, bande, blikkies, glas, toiletafval; oplosbare stowwe soos seep, kunsmis, insekdoders, sure en ander gifstowwe; lewende kieme van toiletafval veroorsaak wateroordraagbare siektes soos diarree

items.bewering: 'n Plastieksak in 'n rivier het nie in die rivier begin nie. Iemand het dit weggegooi, en die wind of die reën het dit tot by die water gebring.
items.blok: Hoe dinge in ons water beland
items.bron: EPA, Nonpoint Source Pollution (epa.gov/nps/basic-information-about-nonpoint-source-nps-pollution): runoff picks up and carries human-made pollutants into rivers and lakes; NOAA Marine Debris material on litter reaching water. Wind-blown and rain-washed litter is the standard route; direct dumping is covered in the next claim.

items.bewering: Reënwater loop oor landerye, strate en vullishope voordat dit in 'n rivier of 'n dam beland. Op pad tel dit grond, afval en ander stowwe op en dra dit saam.
items.blok: Hoe dinge in ons water beland
items.bron: EPA, Polluted Runoff: Nonpoint Source Pollution (epa.gov/nps): 'As the runoff moves, it picks up and carries away natural and human-made pollutants, finally depositing them into lakes, rivers...'; sources listed include agricultural land, urban runoff and sediment.

items.bewering: Afval word soms ook reguit in 'n rivier gegooi.
items.blok: Hoe dinge in ons water beland
items.bron: Stellenbosch epidemiologist Jo Barnes on the Eerste River (IOL, 'The invisible killers in our water', 2013) names dumping into rivers as a cause of pollution; Cape Town and Gauteng reports of objects dumped into the system.

items.bewering: Toiletafval loop in die water in waar 'n rioolpyp lek of oorloop.
items.blok: Hoe dinge in ons water beland
items.bron: Carroll & Curtis, Water SA (Hartbeespoort Dam nutrient mass balance) recommend 'refurbishing leaking and overflowing sewers'; NIVA Hartbeespoort project document names leaking sewers and sewage spills; Mail & Guardian 2023 on collapsing, leaking sewer systems in Gauteng. Note for the writer, not a fault: in South Africa failing sewage treatment works are also a major route (WaterCAN 2025, AfriForum 2023); the sentence does not claim pipes are the only route.

items.bewering: Ons noem dit besoedeling wanneer stowwe of kieme so in water beland en skade doen.
items.blok: Hoe dinge in ons water beland
items.bron: Dictionary.com: 'the contamination of air, water, or soil by substances that are harmful to living organisms'; Collins: 'harmful or poisonous substances introduced into an environment'.

items.bewering: Die eerste soort is onoplosbare stowwe. ... Die tweede soort is oplosbare stowwe ... Die derde soort is kieme.
items.blok: Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien
items.bron: The only 'eerste' in the lesson is an ordinal counting the lesson's own three categories, not a historical or record claim; nothing to verify as a superlative. The three-way division matches the CAPS bullet copied in the lesson (insoluble substances, soluble substances, living germs). No other superlatives (grootste, oudste, enigste, vinnigste) occur in the lesson.

items.bewering: Hulle los nie in water op nie. Hulle bly as stukke of as 'n laag in die water, en jy kan hulle gewoonlik sien.
items.blok: Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien
items.bron: University of Georgia Extension Bulletin B 1523: suspended material such as sand, silt and clay stays in water as particles and is removed by mechanical filtration, unlike dissolved chemicals. 'gewoonlik' correctly covers microplastics and fine particles that are not visible.

items.bewering: Olie meng nie met water nie en vorm 'n laag wat gewoonlik bo-op die water lê.
items.blok: Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien
items.bron: Science Buddies, 'Liquids: miscibility and density': oil and water are immiscible, and 'a mixture where liquids remain physically separate can also be called a heterogeneous mixture'; Frostburg State General Chemistry Online on miscible/immiscible. The layer half is correct: NOAA Office of Response and Restoration, Heavy Fuel Oil fact sheet, shows most oils are lighter than water and float, while some heavy oils suspend or sink, so 'gewoonlik' is right. The fault is in 'meng nie': the lesson's first block sets up 'party dinge net met water meng en ander heeltemal daarin oplos', which puts insoluble things in the 'meng' category, and oil is the CAPS bullet's own first example of something that pollutes by mixing without dissolving. Saying oil 'meng nie met water nie' contradicts that framing inside one lesson, in a topic called Mengsels, and a learner reasoning from it would conclude that oil in water is not a mixture. Science treats it as a mixture (heterogeneous); 'does not mix' is everyday shorthand for 'does not dissolve or blend evenly'.
items.regstelling: Do not say that oil does not mix with water. Say that oil does not dissolve in water and stays apart from it as a separate layer, which usually lies on top of the water. That keeps the oil in the 'net meng' category the first block set up.

items.bewering: Plastiek breek mettertyd in al hoe kleiner stukkies op, maar dit verdwyn nie.
items.blok: Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien
items.bron: NOAA Ocean Service podcast 'Microplastics' (oceanservice.noaa.gov/podcast/june16/dd66-microplastics.html): plastic weathers into smaller and smaller pieces but bacteria cannot break the polymer chains, so it persists; Britannica: 'it doesn't go away. It just spreads out over time.'

items.bewering: Visse, voëls en skilpaaie kan plastiek insluk of daarin vasraak.
items.blok: Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien
items.bron: NOAA Marine Debris fact sheet (via Alaska DEC, 'Plastic Marine Debris'): sea birds, sea turtles and fish eat plastic, and animals become entangled in plastic debris.

items.bewering: Ou bande, blikkies en stukkende glas bly as harde stukke in die water.
items.blok: Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien
items.bron: NOAA Ocean Service (oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/degrade): glass does not degrade; NOAA Marine Debris blog 'The Mystery of How Long Until It's Gone': such items persist for a long time and break down slowly if at all. None of the three dissolves. Minor note, not a fault: steel cans rust over years and tyres are tough rather than hard, but 'harde stukke' as opposed to dissolved matter holds.

items.bewering: By toiletafval is dit die vaste afval self wat nie oplos nie en in die water bly.
items.blok: Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien
items.bron: Britannica, 'sludge', and Wikipedia, 'Sewage sludge': sewage carries suspended faecal solids that settle out as sludge rather than dissolving. Note: those solids decompose over time through bacteria, but they do not dissolve, which is what the sentence contrasts.

items.bewering: Die tweede soort is oplosbare stowwe soos seep en kunsmis.
items.blok: Gif wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: Britannica Kids, micelle/soap entry: soap dissolves in water, forming micelles (Britannica also notes calcium/magnesium soaps in hard water are poorly soluble, an exception that does not affect the claim); EPA nutrient pollution fact sheet: fertiliser nitrogen and phosphorus enter water dissolved in runoff.

items.bewering: Sure, party insekdoders en ander gifstowwe is ook oplosbaar.
items.blok: Gif wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: Wits University, 'The heat of acid mine drainage': mine water becomes acidic and carries dissolved iron, lead and other heavy metals; EPA NPS page lists herbicides and insecticides among runoff pollutants. 'party' rightly covers the fact that some insecticides dissolve poorly in water.

items.bewering: Al hierdie stowwe los in die water op en versprei deur die water. Jy kan hulle dan gewoonlik nie meer sien nie. Water kan dus helder en skoon lyk en steeds besoedel wees.
items.blok: Gif wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: Scientific American, 'Bring Science Home: Separate Solutions', and Science Buddies 'A soluble separation solution': dissolved solids break into particles too small to see; UGA Extension Bulletin B 1523: dissolved chemicals are not removed by mechanical filtration, so clarity does not show safety. 'gewoonlik' covers coloured solutions.

items.bewering: Jy het ook al geleer dat 'n sif, filtreerpapier of 'n lap nie 'n opgeloste stof uit water kan haal nie.
items.blok: Gif wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: UGA Extension Bulletin B 1523: mechanical filters remove sand, silt and clay 'but not dissolved chemicals'; Scientific American 'Separate Solutions': dissolved salt passes through the filter with the water and is recovered by evaporation.

items.bewering: Gifstowwe en sure kan plante en diere in die water skaad of doodmaak.
items.blok: Gif wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: University of Mpumalanga news (2022), 'Acid mine drainage contributes to scarcity of fish species'; mining.com on the WWF-SA/CSIR study: acid drainage acidifies rivers, raises metal levels and kills fish; Wits: acidic metal-rich water is 'toxic to living organisms'.

items.bewering: Mense kan siek word as hulle sulke water drink.
items.blok: Gif wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: AfriForum/TimesLive 2023 and Wits AMD article on toxic metals in water; WHO drinking-water guidance generally. The claim is a 'kan', which holds.

items.bewering: Kunsmis gee plante stowwe wat hulle nodig het om goed te groei, en tog besoedel dit water.
items.blok: Kunsmis laat waterplante te vinnig groei
items.bron: EPA, 'Facts about nutrient pollution' (epa.gov, 2018): nitrogen and phosphorus are nutrients plants need, and too much of them in water is a leading cause of water pollution.

items.bewering: Reën spoel opgeloste kunsmis van landerye en tuine af na riviere en damme.
items.blok: Kunsmis laat waterplante te vinnig groei
items.bron: EPA NPS page: 'excess fertilizers ... from agricultural lands and residential areas' carried by runoff; NIVA Hartbeespoort project document: urban and agricultural runoff feed nutrients into the dam.

items.bewering: In die water laat dit alge en waterplante veel te vinnig groei. Hulle kan dan 'n dam of 'n stil stuk rivier oorgroei.
items.blok: Kunsmis laat waterplante te vinnig groei
items.bron: EPA 'Facts about nutrient pollution': excess nutrients cause algae to grow faster than ecosystems can handle; NIVA Hartbeespoort document and Rhodes University news ('Your sewage is contributing to Hartbeespoort Dam's alien hyacinth invasion'): nutrient enrichment drives algae and water hyacinth that have covered large parts of the dam.

items.bewering: Kieme is nie 'n stof wat oplos of nie oplos nie, maar baie klein lewende dinge.
items.blok: Kieme uit toiletafval
items.bron: CDC, 'Germs that can contaminate tap water', and GIDEON on waterborne diseases: waterborne disease is caused by bacteria, viruses and parasites, i.e. organisms rather than dissolved substances. Classification note: bacteria and protozoa are living things without dispute; whether viruses (e.g. rotavirus, norovirus, major diarrhoea causes) are 'living' is a long-standing definitional debate rather than a fact one source settles. 'Lewende kieme' is the CAPS bullet's own wording, copied into the lesson, so I record this as consistent with CAPS and standard school usage, not as an error.

items.bewering: Toiletafval kan lewende kieme dra.
items.blok: Kieme uit toiletafval
items.bron: Jo Barnes, Stellenbosch (IOL 2013): E. coli in the Eerste River rises from 14 to 34 million per 100 ml downstream of leaking sewage and dumped toilet waste; WaterCAN 2025: E. coli found in nearly two-thirds of sampled rivers.

items.bewering: Kieme is te klein om met jou oë te sien. Water kan dus skoon lyk en tog kieme dra.
items.blok: Kieme uit toiletafval
items.bron: CDC MMWR (Cryptosporidium outbreak in a chlorinated, filtered public water supply, about 13 000 people) and CDC norovirus guidance: microscopic pathogens contaminate water that has been treated and looks clean.

items.bewering: Iemand kan 'n wateroordraagbare siekte soos diarree kry deur sulke water te drink. So 'n siekte kry 'n mens deur water te drink of te gebruik waarin sulke kieme is.
items.blok: Kieme uit toiletafval
items.bron: WHO fact sheet, 'Diarrhoeal disease' (who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/diarrhoeal-disease): spread mainly through contaminated food and drinking water; GIDEON/CDC: waterborne disease comes through drinking water, water used in food preparation, and swimming water, which supports 'drink of gebruik'.

items.bewering: Nie alle diarree kom van kieme in water nie, maar besoedelde water is een manier waarop mense dit kry.
items.blok: Kieme uit toiletafval
items.bron: WHO 'Diarrhoeal disease' fact sheet: infection also spreads through contaminated food and from person to person where hygiene is poor; water is one route among several.

items.bewering: Onoplosbare stowwe bly as stukke of as 'n laag wat jy gewoonlik kan sien.
items.blok: Drie soorte besoedeling in water
items.bron: As for the same claim in 'Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien' (UGA Extension Bulletin B 1523). Read as a set with the other two items: the three are parallel and consistent with each other and with the study blocks.

items.bewering: Oplosbare stowwe los op, en jy kan hulle gewoonlik nie sien nie.
items.blok: Drie soorte besoedeling in water
items.bron: Scientific American 'Separate Solutions'; UGA Extension Bulletin B 1523 (as above).

items.bewering: Kieme is lewende dinge wat te klein is om te sien en mense siek kan maak.
items.blok: Drie soorte besoedeling in water
items.bron: CDC 'Germs that can contaminate tap water'; WHO diarrhoeal disease fact sheet. Same virus classification note as in 'Kieme uit toiletafval'; 'kan' is correctly hedged (not every microbe causes disease).

items.bewering: besoedeling: Iets skadeliks wat in die omgewing beland, soos stowwe of kieme in water, lug of grond.
items.blok: besoedeling
items.bron: Collins (via Dictionary.com): pollution as 'harmful or poisonous substances introduced into an environment'; Dictionary.com: contamination of air, water or soil by harmful substances. The entry uses the 'harmful material' sense where the study text uses the process sense ('wanneer stowwe ... beland en skade doen'); both senses are attested, and read alone the entry is true.

items.bewering: oplosbaar: Iets wat in water kan oplos, soos suiker en sout.
items.blok: oplosbaar
items.bron: Science Buddies, 'A soluble separation solution', and Scientific American, 'Separate Solutions': sugar and salt are standard examples of solids that dissolve in water. Strictly, solubility is relative to a solvent, but the entry names water, so read alone it is true.

items.bewering: onoplosbaar: Iets wat nie in water oplos nie, soos sand.
items.blok: onoplosbaar
items.bron: Science Buddies and Scientific American (as above): sand does not dissolve and is caught by a filter.

items.bewering: kieme: Baie klein lewende dinge wat 'n mens siek kan maak.
items.blok: kieme
items.bron: CDC 'Germs that can contaminate tap water' (bacteria, viruses, parasites). The same note on viruses applies as in 'Kieme uit toiletafval'; the entry follows CAPS's 'lewende kieme'.

items.bewering: wateroordraagbare siekte: 'n Siekte wat 'n mens kan kry deur water te drink of te gebruik waarin kieme is wat mense siek maak.
items.blok: wateroordraagbare siekte
items.bron: GIDEON/CDC: waterborne diseases are contracted through exposure to contaminated drinking water, food-preparation water and swimming water, caused by bacteria, viruses and parasites; WHO diarrhoeal disease fact sheet.

items.bewering: kunsmis: 'n Stof wat mense by grond voeg sodat plante beter groei.
items.blok: kunsmis
items.bron: EPA 'Facts about nutrient pollution': fertilisers supply nitrogen and phosphorus for plant growth on farms and lawns. Fertiliser is also sprayed on leaves or used in hydroponics, but the entry names the common case and does not say it is the only one.

items.bewering: insekdoder: 'n Middel wat mense gebruik om insekte dood te maak.
items.blok: insekdoder
items.bron: EPA NPS page lists insecticides alongside herbicides as pesticides applied on agricultural and residential land; an insecticide is by name and use a product for killing insects.

items.bewering: gifstof: 'n Stof wat 'n lewende ding siek kan maak of kan doodmaak.
items.blok: gifstof
items.bron: Wits, 'The heat of acid mine drainage' (metal-rich acidic water 'toxic to living organisms'); Collins pairs 'harmful or poisonous substances'. A poison is a substance that harms or kills an organism; 'kan' is right.

opsomming: Every claim in the lesson checks out except one: 'Olie meng nie met water nie' contradicts the lesson's own first block, which says some things only mix with water and others dissolve, so it tells a Grade 6 learner in the mixtures topic that oil and water do not make a mixture; it should say oil does not dissolve and stays apart as a layer. There are no analogies and no real superlatives, and the only judgement call (whether viruses count as 'lewende kieme') follows CAPS's own wording and is recorded, not held up.
